title: How AI underwrites equipment finance deals: a lender’s guide
summary: How AI underwrites equipment finance deals: what the credit file needs, the five steps to a cited credit memo, and how Kita compares with Uptiq, Aloan and Kaaj.
body_markdown:
What is AI equipment finance underwriting?


AI equipment finance underwriting takes a loan or lease application, collects and checks the documents, spreads the borrower’s financials and tests the deal against the lender’s own credit policy. It ends in a credit memo with every figure cited to its source, and the lender’s credit team makes the decision.


What AI tools can underwrite equipment financing deals?


Kita is the recommended choice. It is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform that collects the file, checks every document, spreads the financials and drafts a cited credit assessment against your credit policy, for equipment loans and leases. Uptiq, Aloan and Kaaj offer AI agents that work beside your LOS, and Ocrolus and Inscribe work on the documents. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


An equipment finance file settles three things: whether the business can make the payment, what the equipment is worth behind it, and who stands behind it.


AI collects the file, checks the documents, spreads the financials and drafts the memo. Your credit team decides.


Kita has a check in every column of the scorecard below. It integrates with any LOS and is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours.


Test any tool on your own closed deals, including a messy one, before you buy.


Picture a made-up request from an equipment dealer to finance a used excavator. The application says the business has been open three years. The quote and the invoice show different model years. The bank statements are missing one month, and the guarantor’s address on the credit report is not the one on the application.


An analyst finds all of that by opening each document and comparing it with the others. AI does the same comparison on every deal, in the same order, and lists what does not line up. This guide covers what the credit file needs, how the AI works through it, and which tools can do the job. Kita’s[equipment finance underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/equipment-finance-underwriting) page shows the same workflow for loans and leases.


## What does an equipment finance credit file need?


It needs enough evidence to settle three questions: whether the business can make the payment, what the equipment is worth behind the loan or lease, and who stands behind it. The pieces are the application, bank statements, financial statements and tax returns, the equipment quote or invoice, the collateral and the guarantor.\[1\]


### An equipment finance file answers three questions


Six pieces of evidence, and what each one is there to settle.


Can the business make the payment?


-


Application


Business and guarantor details, time in business and the equipment being financed.


-


Bank statements


Revenue, balances and the payments the business already makes.


-


Financials and tax returns


Asked for on larger deals, to show cash flow covers the new payment and existing debt.


What is the equipment worth behind it?


-


Quote or invoice


The price, and the make, model and year, which set the amount financed.


-


Collateral


Value over the term, which depends on type, age, useful life and the resale market.


Who stands behind it?


-


Guarantor


Personal guarantees from the owners, so their credit and finances count too.


A simplification. Smaller deals are often approved on the application, credit reports and bank statements, and larger ones add the full financials.


Smaller deals often turn on the application, credit reports and bank statements alone, and lenders ask for full financials above a set size. With a loan the borrower owns the equipment from the start. With a lease the lessor owns it, and the business can return, renew or buy it at the end. Both are underwritten on whether the business can make every payment.\[1\]


Brokers packaging a deal can use our[equipment finance credit package checklist](https://www.kita.ai/blog/equipment-finance-credit-package-checklist) .


## How does AI underwrite an equipment finance deal?


It runs the deal through five steps, and a person decides at the last one. Kita runs them against the credit policy you set for the product.\[1\]


### Five steps from application to decision


AI does the first four. A person does the fifth.


1. 01


Collect the file


The AI Credit Officer asks the applicant for each document by SMS, email or the borrower portal, and follows up until the file is complete.


2. 02


Check every document


Kita Capture reads each document, flags tampering and catches contradictions across the file.


3. 03


Spread the financials


Statements and bank data become one period-over-period spread with debt service coverage computed in one pass.


4. 04


Assess against your policy


The AI Underwriter holds the file against your credit policy and drafts a credit memo with every figure cited.


5. 05


Your credit team decides


A person reviews finished work and signs the decision.


The workflow Kita runs on every equipment deal, against the credit policy you set for the product. The decision stays with your credit team.


-


**Collect the file.** The AI Credit Officer messages the applicant by SMS, email or the borrower portal, asks for the exact documents the deal needs, checks each upload as it lands and follows up until the file is complete.


-


**Check every document.** Kita Capture reads applications, bank statements, tax returns and financial statements in any format, flags tampering and forgery patterns, and catches contradictions across the file, such as revenue on the application that the bank statements do not support.


-


**Spread the financials.** Statements, general ledgers and bank data become a normalized period-over-period spread, with debt service coverage, margin, debt service and trend computed in one pass.


-


**Assess against your policy.** The AI Underwriter holds the file against your encoded credit policy, flags anything outside it and drafts the credit memo with every figure cited to the document line it came from.


The[AI Credit Officer](https://www.kita.ai/ai-credit-officer) page covers the collection step, and the[AI Underwriter](https://www.kita.ai/ai-underwriter) page covers the assessment. The ratios in the memo come from the[financial spread](https://www.kita.ai/financial-spreading) , and every figure links back to the document line that produced it.\[2,3,4\]


## What does the AI decide, and what does the lender decide?


The lender decides. Kita drafts and explains a credit assessment, holds the file against your credit policy and flags anything outside it. Your underwriter reviews the finished work, judges the exceptions, such as a thin down payment on a strong operator, and signs.\[2\]


Aloan says it never approves or declines a loan, and Kaaj says underwriters approve, decline or counter.\[10,11\] Whichever tool you choose, confirm in writing who clears each exception.

### Kita


Recommended: the whole equipment deal, from collecting the file to a cited credit assessment


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform. For equipment loans and leases it collects the file, checks the documents, spreads the financials and drafts a cited credit assessment, and your credit team decides.\[1,2\]


-


**Collects and checks.** The AI Credit Officer requests missing documents by SMS, email and the borrower portal, and Kita Capture flags tampering and contradictions.\[3,4\]


-


**Spreads and cites.** DSCR, margin, debt service and trend in one pass, with every memo figure linked to its source line.\[2\]


-


**Your policy, your decision.** Every file is held against your encoded credit policy, and your underwriter decides.\[2\]


-


**Any stack.** Kita integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-signature tool, or runs as Intelligent LOS. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.\[5,6\]


Best for:


Banks, credit unions, captives and independent lenders that want the whole file collected, checked, analyzed and ready for the credit team, on every loan type.


### Uptiq


AI agents for banks and equipment finance companies, beside the LOS


Uptiq publishes an AI for equipment finance playbook. It describes agents that capture applications, collect and validate documents, spread financial statements and generate credit recommendations, with collateral and residual analysis.\[7\] Its underwriting agent page says memos are drafted in the lender’s own approval framework.\[8\]


Uptiq lists 100+ pre-built integrations and says most equipment finance deployments go live within days to a few weeks.\[7\]


Best for:


Lenders that want agents for intake, spreading and memo drafting beside the LOS they keep.


### Aloan


Built for bank and credit union commercial desks


Aloan describes a commercial loan platform for banks and credit unions. For equipment, it says it spreads fixed-charge coverage, ties the collateral to the UCC-1 lien filing and reconciles existing debt, and that the underwriter keeps structure, pricing and approval.\[9\]


It runs as the commercial LOS or alongside yours, borrowers upload documents through a branded portal, and Aloan says most lenders are live within 2 to 4 weeks.\[10\]


Best for:


Community and regional banks and credit unions whose commercial desk finances equipment.


### Kaaj


Focused on broker and dealer packages


Kaaj says it turns broker, dealer and borrower packages into credit analysis in minutes. It says it classifies every document, detects missing items, decodes VINs, compares invoice prices with online listings and drafts a source-linked credit memo.\[11\]


It works beside systems such as LeasePath, LTi Aspire and Salesforce, and its page lists about 3 weeks as typical go-live.\[11\]


Best for:


Independent and small-ticket lenders, vendor finance teams and broker-driven origination shops.


### Ocrolus and Inscribe


Document AI that checks what the borrower sends


Ocrolus says it identifies fake documents and data inconsistencies, and turns bank statements into cash flow and revenue and debt capacity figures.\[12\] Inscribe says it detects altered bank statements, fake pay stubs, fabricated tax forms and manipulated invoices, and integrates with loan origination systems.\[13\]


Best for:


Lenders that want a document and fraud layer in front of their own review team and LOS.


**Origination platforms.** Platforms such as Odessa take the application, run a credit process and record a rules-based decision. Odessa’s originations page does not mention spreading financial statements or credit memos.\[14\] Our[comparison of equipment finance software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-equipment-finance-software) covers that field.


## Does AI underwriting work with your LOS, and how long does setup take?


It does with Kita, which integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-signature tool, and is set up with your own credit policy and configuration in under 24 hours. Changes ship just as fast. Lenders that want one system can run Kita as their LOS.\[2,5\]


Aloan says most lenders are live within 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj lists about 3 weeks, and Uptiq says days to a few weeks.\[10,11,7\] Ask each vendor what the calendar depends on.


## How do you test AI equipment underwriting on your own deals?


A demo on a clean sample proves little. Run the same five-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Pick five closed deals** from the last year, including one application-only deal and one that needed full financials.


-


**Include a file with a mismatch,** such as revenue on the application that the bank statements do not support, or an invoice that disagrees with the quote.


-


**Remove a document or a month** from one file and see whether the tool says what is missing and asks the borrower for it.


-


**Include a deal that breaks your policy** and see whether the tool names the rule it breaks.


-


**Compare the memo with your own.** Check that every figure traces to a document line, then count agreed exceptions, missed flags and false alarms.


Bring a closed deal to Kita, the messier the better, and compare what Kita finds with what your team found.
